title: منظمات حقوقية: إيران نفذت أكثر من ألف عملية إعدام هذا العام - الوطن
content: Human rights organizations report that Iran has carried out more than 1,000 executions in 2025, the highest number recorded in over 15 years. The organizations attribute the surge to the use of the death penalty as a political tool to suppress dissent, particularly following the 2022 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests and heightened tensions with Israel in June 2025. Executions have increased notably in cases involving national and religious minorities, including Baloch, Kurds, and Afghans, with the number of Afghans executed rising from 25 in 2023 to over 80 in 2024 and continuing to rise in 2025. Women, such as Kurdish activists Pashkhan Azizi and political dissident Roshan Maradi, have also faced execution sentences, described by rights groups as unjust and part of a broader campaign targeting women in civil and political activism. Many executions are based on vague charges like 'moharebeh' (enmity against God), 'efsad fil arz' (corruption on earth), and espionage, with at least ten men executed since June 2025 on political charges, including eight accused of spying for Israel. Drug-related executions persist despite international opposition to the death penalty for non-violent offenses, with rights advocates asserting these cases serve as a cover for broader repression. The judiciary, particularly revolutionary courts, is criticized for lacking independence, conducting secret trials, and denying defendants fundamental rights, as seen in the case of Afghan citizen Babak Shabazi, executed in September 2025 despite allegations of torture. Organizations urge the international community to impose immediate political and economic pressure on Iran, use universal jurisdiction to prosecute officials, and demand a moratorium on executions as a first step toward abolition. They emphasize that the continued use of capital punishment constitutes a grave violation of the right to life under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and entrenches a culture of impunity. A comprehensive judicial reform is called for to ensure independence from security agencies and fair trials.

title: إيران تعدم أكثر من ألف شخص منذ بداية العام
content: According to a report released by the human rights organization Hanja, Iran has executed more than 1,000 people since the beginning of 2024. The report states that 404 executions have taken place since the war between Iran and Israel erupted in June, a 40 % increase from the period before the conflict and the largest rise in two decades, the organization said. It added that executions had never exceeded 1,000 in a short period before, writing, 'لم تتجاوز حالات الإعدام ألف حالة من قبل خلال فترة قصيرة'. By the end of August, the United Nations had already recorded 841 executions in Iran, a sharp rise compared with previous years. UN data for 2024 show 975 executions, suggesting the total for the year could reach the highest level in decades.

title: Horror 'mass killing campaign' executed 9 people day by hanging
content: Iran has carried out its highest number of executions in more than three decades, with at least 1,000 people executed over the past nine months, according to the Norway‑based Iran Human Rights organisation (IHR). The mass‑killing campaign of hangings ran from January to September, surpassing the 975 executions recorded in 2024 and marking the highest figure since IHR began its records 17 years ago. IHR activists reported that 64 executions occurred in the last week alone, averaging more than nine hangings a day. The organisation says the lack of transparency and reporting restrictions likely mean the true number is higher. IHR director Mahmood Amiry‑Moghaddam warned that the "mass killing campaign" in Iran’s prisons is expanding daily and that the widespread, arbitrary executions without due process amount to crimes against humanity, calling for it to become a top priority for the international community.

title: Iran: Further Information: Thousands at risk of execution in Iran - Amnesty International
content: According to Amnesty International, Iran is facing an execution crisis that has reached horrific proportions. Thousands of people are at risk of execution after being sentenced to death, including for drug‑related offences or for vaguely worded charges following grossly unfair trials. Since the 2022 Woman Life Freedom uprising, Iranian authorities have weaponised the death penalty as a tool of oppression, with 'over 800 people executed thus far in 2025 alone.'

title: Iran has executed at least 1,000 people in 2025 - NGO
content: According to the Norway‑based Iran Human Rights (IHR) group, Iran has executed at least 1,000 people in 2025, the highest figure since IHR began recording in 2008. The group reported 64 executions in the past week alone, averaging more than nine hangings per day, and noted that the 975 executions recorded last year were surpassed. IHR director Mahmood Amiry‑Moghaddam said the executions 'amount to crimes against humanity and must be placed at the top of the international community's agenda.' The organization also warned that its figures are an absolute minimum, likely higher due to lack of transparency. Iran carries out executions exclusively by hanging, with most taking place in prison, and human rights groups such as Amnesty International rank Iran as the world's second most prolific executioner after China. The article quotes the NGO as saying 'In recent months the Islamic republic has begun a mass killing campaign in Iran's prisons, the dimensions of which -- in the absence of serious international reactions -- are expanding every day,' and that 'Any dialogue between countries committed to the foundations of human rights and the Islamic republic that does not include the execution crisis in Iran is unacceptable.'

title: IRAN. 187 prisonniers exécutés en septembre – Kurdistan au féminin
content: At least 187 prisoners were executed in Iranian prisons in September 2025, marking the highest monthly total in two decades and a 140% increase compared to 78 executions in September 2024. According to data compiled by the human rights organization Hengaw, 181 of the executed individuals have been identified, while six remain under verification. Among those executed were three political prisoners—Mehran Bahramian from Semirom, Babak Shahbazi from Karaj, and Bahman Choubi-Asl—and two prisoners of conscience: Mohammad Kashfi from Bandar Khamir and Eskandar Bazmandegan from Khur in Fars Province. Of the total executions, 90 were for 'premeditated murder' (49% of the total), and 92 were related to drug-related offenses. At least 14 executions were carried out in secret, without notification to families or last visits. The ethnic breakdown shows 35 Kurds (19%), 23 Lors (12%), 15 Turks, 14 Baloch, 8 Gilaks, 4 Arabs, 10 Afghans, 57 from Fars Province, and 21 of unconfirmed ethnic origin. Only eight executions were reported by state or judiciary-affiliated media, representing about 4% of the total, indicating widespread underreporting. The data is sourced from Hengaw, a rights monitoring organization, and published on kurdistan-au-feminin.fr on October 3, 2025.

title: В Иране за последний год казнили более 1 500 человек
content: Between October 10, 2024, and October 8, 2025, Iran carried out 1,537 executions, according to a report by the Telegram channel 'Free Iran' citing the Iranian Human Rights Organization. This marks an 86% increase compared to the previous year, with 94% of executions conducted in secret, without notifying families or the public. Among those executed were three minors and 49 women, eight of whom were publicly hanged. The most common charges were drug trafficking (48.3% of cases) and murder (43.5%). The highest number of executions occurred in the provinces of Alborz, Isfahan, and Fars. Since the beginning of 2025, 1,106 people have been executed, including 30 women.

title: Iran’s Executions in August Jump 70 Percent Compared to Previous Year as Rights Groups Warn of Troubling Surge
content: The Islamic regime in Iran accelerated its execution machine in August 2024, carrying out at least 152 executions, a 70 percent increase over the 94 executions recorded in August 2023, according to the Hengaw Organization for Human Rights. Hengaw identified 148 of the executed individuals, leaving four unnamed. Among those executed were Roozbeh Vadi, accused of ‘espionage for Israel,’ and Mehdi Asgharzadeh, an alleged ISIS member. The regime also executed at least five women for murder and one woman on drug charges. Two or more executions were carried out publicly in Beyram and Kordkuy. HRANA reported that Iran routinely forces confessions from political and ideological defendants, broadcasting them on state television; in 2024 HRANA documented 28 forced‑confession cases, and this month state television aired the forced confessions of a group of Christian converts. HRANA also recorded 73 arrests last month for citizens expressing political views, and the state sentenced 27 people to 658 months in prison, 132 months of exile, and 130 lashes for speech offenses. United Nations spokeswoman Ravina Shamdasani warned that the high number of executions indicates a systematic pattern of using the death penalty as a tool of state intimidation, with disproportionate targeting of ethnic minorities and migrants. She stated, 'The high number of executions indicates a systematic pattern of using the death penalty as a tool of state intimidation, with disproportionate targeting of ethnic minorities and migrants,' and added, 'Public executions add an extra layer of outrage upon human dignity … not only on the dignity of the people concerned, the people who are executed, but also on all those who have to bear witness.' Shamdasani further warned that 'the psychological trauma of bearing witness to somebody being hanged in public, particularly for children, is unacceptable' and argued that the death penalty 'should never be imposed for conduct that is protected under international human rights law.' Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the situation as 'extraordinary and dangerous acts of aggression orchestrated by a foreign nation on Australian soil.'

title: Exécutions en Iran : Un Bilan Meurtrier en 2025
content: Iran recorded over 1,176 confirmed executions by the end of September 2025, according to international reports including Amnesty International, making it the world leader in executions for the year—surpassing all other countries. More than half of the executions were linked to drug-related offenses, with nearly 40% related to murder (qisas), and a smaller but impactful number tied to political and security-related charges. Victims included 39 women, political prisoners such as Behrouz Ehsani, Mehdi Hassani, Mehran Bahramian, Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, Vahid Bani Amerian, Abolhassan Montazer Akbar Daneshvarkar, Mohammad Taghavi Pouya Ghobadi, and Babak Alipour, as well as members of ethnic minorities and juvenile offenders. Executions were carried out in secret, typically at dawn, without notification to families, lawyers, or last visits—violating the right to a fair trial and the right to be informed. The practice is systemic, with prisons such as Qezel Hesar (Karaj), Vakilabad (Mashhad), and Adelabad (Shiraz) serving as execution centers. The use of the death penalty is described as a tool of state intimidation and social control, disproportionately targeting the poor, women, political dissidents, and ethnic minorities. International human rights figures, including UN High Commissioner Volker Türk and UN Special Rapporteur Mai Sato, have called for an immediate moratorium on executions, the annulment of death sentences for political prisoners, and an end to executions for drug offenses, which violate Iran’s international obligations. The report concludes that Iran’s death penalty system is a permanent instrument of repression, not justice, and constitutes the bloodiest period in three decades.

title: Iran executes at least 1,000 people in 'mass killing campaign'
content: Iran has carried out at least 1,000 executions in a 'mass killing campaign' between January and September 2025, according to the Norway‑based Iran Human Rights organisation (IHR). The organisation reports that 64 people were executed in the past week alone, averaging more than nine hangings per day. These figures already exceed the 975 executions recorded in 2024 and represent the highest total since IHR began tracking executions in 2008.
